summary: Steel tower in Washington County, NC, begun by the CCC in April 1936 and completed by Camp P-67 on August 13, 1936; no source read describes the site today.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Erection begun by the CCC in April 1936; construction completed by members of Camp P-67 on August 13, 1936, per the Forest Lookouts entry.

evidence.supports: erection begun April 1936 by the CCC; 99-foot 9-inch steel tower; cost funded through Emergency Conservation Works
evidence.quote: April 1936: The erection of a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower was begun by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the $1,770.21 cost was funded through the Emergency Conservation Works program.

evidence.supports: construction completed August 13, 1936 by Camp P-67
evidence.quote: August 13, 1936: The construction of the tower was completed by members of Camp P-67 of the CCC.

notes_for_editor: Two sources only: the Forest Lookouts North Carolina summary (dates, size, cost program, completing camp) and the tnlandforms list (county, coordinates). The Forest Lookouts page cites the August 1936 entry to the 7th Biennial Report with the year printed as 1038, probably a typo for 1938; the story does not repeat that citation. A Facebook group post asking whether an abandoned fire tower near the Roanoke River in Plymouth is still there was seen only as a search snippet; it could not be opened, so it is not cited, and it does not establish whether the tower survives. No source read gives a later history, staffing, fires or the site today. The shared web-search budget for this run was exhausted before fate or present-day condition could be searched, and no other route was used. Not on FFLOS or in the cached NHLR North Carolina list. The record's agency field was null and is filled from the Forest Lookouts entry.
